takeaway: Venous ulcers sit in the gaiter area; treat with elevation and compression bandaging, and exclude coexisting arterial disease.

question.text: A 74-year-old man has a long history of bilateral leg ulceration. Which statement regarding venous ulcers is correct?

lines.text: A venous ulcer sits in the gaiter area, around the ankle, with a sloughy base.
The skin around it can be dark and hard, from lipodermatosclerosis.
Treatment starts with elevation. Raise the leg, and the happy vein drains.
Regular dressings and compression bandaging do the rest.
But always check the pedal pulses first, because compression can further compromise a poor blood supply.
So elevation aids treatment, and that is our answer.
lines.say: (clears throat) So elevation aids treatment, and that is our answer.
